newsitem.title: COMOROS: Hijack plane death toll rise to 59.
newsitem.headline: Hijack plane death toll rise to 59.

text.p: The death toll from the hijacked Ethiopian Airlines plane that crashed into the sea off the Comoro Islands has risen to 59, a medical source said on Sunday.
Witnesses said bodies of some of the dead had been washed ashore along the island coast. One body, that of a female, had been cut in two, the witnesses said.
A spokeswoman for Ethiopian Airlines said earlier on Sunday that there were 58 dead and 52 survivors, with 65 people still unaccounted for.
Witnesses said the plane had split into three pieces. The cockpit was not visible, but the rest of the plane, split into two, could be seen now that the tide had gone out.

It was now possible to walk to the wreckage, but lines of police from the gendarmerie were keeping onlookers away, the witnesses said. The plane was estimated to be no more than 500 metres (yards) off the coast of the idyllic tropical island.

Bodies were being washed ashore along stretches of palm-covered beaches, according to witnesses. They were being taken to a cold storage facility that formerly belonged to a state-owned company that imported meat into the islands.
